stem.text: The boiling point of water, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is higher than that of hydrogen sulfide, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.
Which statement explains this difference in boiling points?

A.text: The bond energy of $\text{O–H}$ is greater than the bond energy of $\text{S–H}$.

B.text: The intermolecular forces in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ are weaker than the intermolecular forces in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.

C.text: The $\text{S–H}$ bond in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is longer than the $\text{O–H}$ bond in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

D.text: There is significant intermolecular hydrogen bonding in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ but **not** in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.
